faq.q: How much does an Estepona hen party boat charter cost in 2046?
faq.a: Tier A boats (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) start at €749 for 2 hours and go up to €2,299 for 8 hours. Tier B (Mangusta 80) is €4,719 minimum for 4 hours, including a free jet ski. All prices include skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT. For other boats, request a quote via WhatsApp.

faq.q: Which boat is best for a hen party of 10–12 people?
faq.a: For up to 12 guests, the Mangusta 80 (24m) or Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m) are excellent. Both have spacious flybridges, sun pads, and shaded saloons. The Mangusta 80 also includes a jet ski for extra fun. For a smaller group of 10, the Pershing 46 (14m) or Fairline Targa 12m work well.

faq.q: What is included in the hen party charter price?
faq.a: Every charter includes a licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish VAT (21%). No hidden fees. You can add a DJ, photographer, or prosecco tower at extra cost – just ask via WhatsApp.

faq.q: Can we bring our own decorations or food?
faq.a: Yes, you can bring hen party decorations like banners, balloons, and tableware – just avoid confetti that can be difficult to clean. Food is welcome; many groups bring a catered platter or cake. The boat has a fridge and basic glassware. No glass bottles on the swimming platform, please.

faq.q: What is the best time of year for a hen party boat charter in Estepona?
faq.a: May through October offers the best weather: sea temperatures 18–25°C and air temperatures 22–32°C. July and August are hottest and busiest – book at least 3–6 months ahead. For lower rates and quieter marinas, consider late May, June, or September.

faq.q: Do we need to bring anything for the day?
faq.a: Bring swimwear, towels, sunscreen (reef-safe preferred), sunglasses, a hat, and a light jacket for the evening. The boat provides life jackets and safety gear. If you plan to use the jet ski on the Mangusta 80, bring a change of clothes. A waterproof phone pouch is handy for photos.

faq.q: Can we swim and anchor during the charter?
faq.a: Absolutely. The skipper will anchor at calm spots like Cala del Faro, Cala Cortés, or near the Estepona coastline. You can swim, use the paddleboard (available on some boats), or take the jet ski out. Swimming stops are usually 30–60 minutes depending on your itinerary.

faq.q: How do we book an Estepona hen party boat charter?
faq.a: Contact us via WhatsApp or the website. Provide your preferred date, group size, and budget. We’ll recommend a boat and send a quote. A deposit (usually 50%) secures the booking, with the balance due 7 days before departure. Cancellation terms are shared at booking.

data.body_html:
Planning an Estepona hen party boat charter 2046? You're looking at a day of sun, swimming, and celebration along the Costa del Sol. This breakdown covers real costs — from €749 for a 2-hour trip — boat options, what's included, and how to keep the party smooth. No fluff, just numbers and honest advice.

Why choose a boat charter for an Estepona hen party?

Estepona's coastline offers calm waters, hidden coves like Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés, and a relaxed vibe away from the Puerto Banús crowds. A private charter gives your group total freedom: swim stops, music, and privacy. All boats depart from Puerto Banús, just 10 minutes by car from Estepona centre. The Estepona hen party boat charter 2046 market is competitive, but our fleet offers clear pricing with no surprises.

Budget breakdown: what you'll actually pay

Our boats fall into two pricing tiers. Tier A (Astondoa 40, Azimut 39) costs €749 for 2 hours, €1,299 for 4 hours, €1,799 for 6 hours, or €2,299 for 8 hours. Tier B (Mangusta 80, both white and grey) starts at €4,719 for a minimum 4-hour charter and includes a free jet ski. For all other boats — like the Ferretti 94, Canados 86, or Maiora 26m — pricing is on request via WhatsApp. Every price includes the skipper, fuel, drinks, snacks, insurance, and 21% VAT. No hidden fees.

Extra costs you might consider: a DJ (€300–€500), photographer (€250–€400), prosecco tower (€150–€250), or a catered paella platter (€20–€30 per person). These are optional and arranged on request.

Which boat fits your hen party size?

Hen parties range from intimate groups of 5 to full-on 12-person celebrations. Here's a quick guide:

  • 5–6 guests: Dubhe (8m, 5 pax) or Mariah SX21 (6.4m, 5 pax) — cosy and budget-friendly.
  • 8–10 guests: Pershing 46 (14m, 10 pax), Fairline Targa 12m (12m, 10 pax), or Lagoon 380 (11.6m, 10 pax).
  • 10–12 guests: Mangusta 80 (24m, 12 pax), Azimut 58 Flybridge (17.6m, 12 pax), or Ferretti 94 (29m, 12 pax) — plenty of deck space for dancing and sunbathing.

For a classic hen party with a jet ski, the Mangusta 80 is a popular pick. The flybridge on the Azimut 58 gives panoramic views and a second lounge area.

What's included — and what's not

Included on every charter: licensed skipper, fuel, water, soft drinks, beer, white wine, cava, light snacks, insurance, safety equipment, and Spanish IVA (21%). You can bring your own decorations and food. The boat provides glassware and a fridge. Not included: DJ, photographer, prosecco tower, or premium spirits — these can be added for an extra fee. No hidden charges for cleaning or docking.

Tips for a flawless hen party day

  • Book early: Peak season (July–August) fills up 3–6 months ahead. May, June, and September offer better availability and slightly cooler temps.
  • Plan your itinerary: Tell the skipper your preferred swimming spots. Cala del Faro and Cala Cortés are sheltered and beautiful. You can also cruise past the Marbella Golden Mile and La Concha mountain backdrop.
  • Pack smart: Swimwear, towels, sunscreen (reef-safe), hats, sunglasses, and a light jacket for the evening breeze. A waterproof phone case is handy for photos.
  • Consider a half-day (4 hours): This gives you time for a swim stop, lunch, and some cruising. Full-day (8 hours) includes a longer lunch and multiple anchorages.
  • Check the weather: The skipper monitors conditions and may adjust the route. In case of rough seas, you can reschedule or cancel per our terms.

Sample itinerary for a 4-hour hen party charter

TimeActivity
14:00Board at Puerto Banús, welcome cava
14:15Safety briefing & departure
14:30–15:15Cruise towards Estepona coast, music playing
15:15–16:00Swim stop at Cala del Faro, jet ski (if Mangusta 80)
16:00–16:45Lunch & drinks on board
16:45–17:30Return cruise to Puerto Banús
17:30Disembark

This is a flexible template — your skipper can adjust based on your group's energy and preferences.

How to book your Estepona hen party boat charter 2046

Contact us via WhatsApp or the website with your preferred date, group size, and budget. We'll recommend a boat and send a detailed quote. A 50% deposit secures the booking, with the balance due 7 days before departure. Cancellation terms are provided at booking. For more inspiration, check our boat rental Marbella guide.
